identification.summary: GOBLIN PANDA is CrowdStrike's name for a China-linked espionage actor also tracked as Cycldek and Conimes, focused mainly on Southeast Asia, above all Vietnam [S1][S3][S4]. CrowdStrike says its targets have mostly been in the defense, energy and government sectors [S1][S2]. Kaspersky describes Cycldek as a Chinese-speaking APT that targets high-profile entities in Southeast Asia and judges it more capable than its reputation suggests [S3][S6].
identification.firstObserved: CrowdStrike first observed GOBLIN PANDA activity in September 2013 [S1][S2]. Kaspersky reports Cycldek activity since at least 2013 and code lineage back to 2014 [S3][S6].
identification.notes: Microsoft has no storm-name mapping recorded in this record (msName is empty). Kaspersky and some secondary sources list APT 27 as an alias of Cycldek; Microsoft maps APT27 to Linen/Circle Typhoon, so that alias is not adopted here (see gaps). Kaspersky splits NewCore malware into BlueCore and RedCore variants linked to two sub-clusters that share code and infrastructure and may be offshoots of one larger entity [S3][S4][S6].

attribution.confidence: Vendors label the actor Chinese-speaking or China-linked (CrowdStrike, Kaspersky) [S1][S3][S6]. No government attribution or sponsoring organization was found in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Vendor telemetry and malware analysis by CrowdStrike (2018) and Kaspersky (2020), including code and infrastructure overlap between malware clusters [S1][S3][S6].

objectives: Espionage against government, defense and energy entities in Southeast Asia, with theft of data including from air-gapped systems via USB media [S1][S2][S4][S5].

targeting.notes: CrowdStrike reports defense, energy and government targeting, with Vietnamese-language decoys in 2018; C2 indicators pointed to Laos though Laotian targets were not confirmed [S1][S2]. Kaspersky reported government targets in Vietnam, Thailand and Laos [S4][S5]. Central Asia targeting could not be verified and was removed.

capabilities.summary: 2018 spear-phishing used Vietnamese-language Word decoys exploiting CVE-2012-0158 to drop the side-loading implant CrowdStrike calls QCRat [S1][S2]. Kaspersky's 2020 research described the NewCore RAT (BlueCore and RedCore variants; RedCore adds a keylogger and RDP logger) and USBCulprit, a tool that exfiltrates data via USB media and is relevant to air-gapped networks [S3][S4][S5][S6]. CrowdStrike lists PlugX and HttpTunnel as the actor's primary malware [S1]; other reporting lists and CVE-2017-11882 and CVE-2018-0802 as additional Office exploits; these were seen only in search-result summaries [S2][S5].

campaigns.name: First observed activity
campaigns.summary: CrowdStrike dates its first observation of GOBLIN PANDA to September 2013 [S1].

campaigns.name: Vietnam decoy-document campaign
campaigns.summary: CrowdStrike observed new Vietnam-focused activity in July 2018 (reported in its August 2018 post): Vietnamese-language Word decoys with training themes exploiting CVE-2012-0158 and dropping QCRat; C2 indicators pointed to Laos but Laotian targets were not confirmed [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: Kaspersky Cycldek report (USBCulprit, NewCore)
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky disclosed USBCulprit for USB-based exfiltration and the BlueCore and RedCore NewCore variants, with victims in Vietnam, Thailand and Laos [S3][S4][S5][S6].

diamond.adversary: Chinese-speaking espionage actor tracked as GOBLIN PANDA, Cycldek and Conimes; sponsor not established in gathered sources [S1][S3].
diamond.capability: Office exploit spear-phishing, QCRat, NewCore (BlueCore/RedCore) and USBCulprit [S1][S4][S6].
diamond.infrastructure: C2 indicators pointing to Laos were observed in 2018; Kaspersky notes shared code and infrastructure across clusters. Detailed infrastructure was not reviewed [S1][S6].
diamond.victim: Government, military, defense and energy organizations, mainly in Vietnam, plus Thailand and Laos [S1][S4][S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: CrowdStrike reports heavy activity in late spring and early summer 2014 during South China Sea tensions, which suggests regional strategic-intelligence tasking (analyst inference) [S1].
diamond.technology: Legacy Microsoft Office vulnerabilities, removable USB media and air-gapped networks [S1][S4].

gaps: WebFetch could not reach securelist.com, crowdstrike.com or fortinet.com (DNS failure); findings rest on search-result summaries and secondary coverage, not the primary reports. Primary documents not opened: Kaspersky 'Cycldek: Bridging the air-gap', CrowdStrike August 2018 post, Fortinet playbook, CrowdStrike 2020 Global Threat Report, Thales 2022 handbook.
No reporting dated after 2020 was found in searches; current activity level is unknown.
State sponsor, tasking organization and any government attribution are not established in gathered sources.
Naming conflict: Kaspersky and secondary sources list APT 27 as a Cycldek alias, but Microsoft maps APT27 to Linen/Circle Typhoon. Do not merge these clusters without primary evidence.
No MITRE ATT&CK group ID or Microsoft storm name is recorded for this actor.
Initial access beyond Office-exploit lures, and exact victim counts, are not documented in the sources gathered.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is regional government, defense and energy networks in Vietnam, Thailand and Laos, including air-gapped enclaves reachable by removable media [S4][S5]. STEP 2: The actor reuses old Office exploits, so unpatched legacy Office installations are the exposed surface [S1][S2]. STEP 3: Observed pattern is localized-language spear-phishing, then side-loaded implant (QCRat/NewCore), then USB-based collection (USBCulprit) [S1][S4][S6]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued regional government and defense espionage. MDCOA is USB-borne collection against partner or coalition air-gapped systems during regional crisis. Candidate indicators: Vietnamese-language decoy documents, DLL side-loading by signed binaries, and unexpected USB-resident executables [S1][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track regional partner-nation government and defense incidents attributable to Cycldek/GOBLIN PANDA. (2) Authorities: partner-network support depends on host-nation agreements; pursue through established channels. (3) Mission assurance: enforce removable-media controls and legacy Office patching on enclaves supporting regional operations [S1][S4]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partners and reconcile vendor names (GOBLIN PANDA, Cycldek, Conimes) in reporting [S1][S3].

provenance.importedSummary: Goblin Panda is one of a handful of elite Chinese advanced persistent threat (APT) groups. Most Chinese APTs target the United States and NATO, but Goblin Panda focuses primarily on Southeast Asia.
